claim: During macroautophagy, cytoplasmic constituents are engulfed by autophagosomes.
source: During macroautophagy, cytoplasmic constituents are engulfed by autophagosomes.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about macroautophagy that is stated in the abstract.

claim: Lysosomes fuse with closed autophagosomes but not with unclosed intermediate structures.
source: Lysosomes fuse with closed autophagosomes but not with unclosed intermediate structures.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the abstract.

claim: The late recruitment of the autophagosomal SNARE syntaxin 17 (STX17) to mature autophagosomes achieves temporal regulation of autophagosome-lysosome fusion.
source: This is achieved in part by the late recruitment of the autophagosomal SNARE syntaxin 17 (STX17) to mature autophagosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known mechanism and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: The temporally regulated recruitment of STX17 depends on the positively charged C-terminal region of STX17.
source: Here, we show that this temporally regulated recruitment of STX17 depends on the positively charged C-terminal region of STX17.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study presented in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 1D and 1E.

claim: Mature autophagosomes are more negatively charged compared with unclosed intermediate structures.
source: Consistent with this finding, mature autophagosomes are more negatively charged compared with unclosed intermediate structures.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data using charge probes shown in Figure 2.

claim: The electrostatic maturation of autophagosomes is likely driven by the accumulation of phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI4P) in the autophagosomal membrane.
source: This electrostatic maturation of autophagosomes is likely driven by the accumulation of phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI4P) in the autophagosomal membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 3 showing PI4P accumulation.

claim: Dephosphorylation of autophagosomal PI4P prevents the association of STX17 to autophagosomes.
source: Accordingly, dephosphorylation of autophagosomal PI4P prevents the association of STX17 to autophagosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vitro experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Molecular dynamics simulations support PI4P-dependent membrane insertion of the transmembrane helices of STX17.
source: Furthermore, molecular dynamics simulations support PI4P-dependent membrane insertion of the transmembrane helices of STX17.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by simulation data shown in Figure 5.

claim: STX17 is recruited immediately before or after the closure of autophagosomes.
source: One is the regulated translocation of the autophagosomal SNARE syntaxin 17 (STX17), which is recruited immediately before or after the closure of autophagosomes (Itakura et al., 2012; Takáts et al., 2013; Tsuboyama et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: YKT6 is a conserved autophagosomal SNARE that is activated during autophagosome maturation.
source: The other is the activation of YKT6, a conserved autophagosomal SNARE (Matsui et al., 2018), which is kept inactivated by ULK1 (a homolog of yeast Atg1)-mediated phosphorylation until the completion of autophagosome formation (ULK1/Atg1 is dissociated at this time; Barz et al., 2020; Essmann et al., 1995; Sánchez-Martín et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: STX17 interacts with SNAP29 and the lysosomal SNARE protein VAMP7 or VAMP8 to mediate autophagosome-lysosome fusion.
source: Then, STX17 interacts with SNAP29 and the lysosomal SNARE protein VAMP7 or VAMP8, and YKT6 interacts with SNAP29 and the lysosomal STX7 to mediate the fusion between autophagosomes and lysosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: YKT6 interacts with SNAP29 and the lysosomal STX7 to mediate autophagosome-lysosome fusion.
source: Then, STX17 interacts with SNAP29 and the lysosomal SNARE protein VAMP7 or VAMP8, and YKT6 interacts with SNAP29 and the lysosomal STX7 to mediate the fusion between autophagosomes and lysosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: LC3/GABARAP family proteins and immunity-related GTPase M (IRGM) are involved in autophagosomal recruitment of STX17 according to one study.
source: A previous study reported that LC3/GABARAP family proteins and immunity-related GTPase M (IRGM) are involved in autophagosomal recruitment of STX17 (Kumar et al., 2018a), whereas other studies have shown that LC3/GABARAP family proteins are not required (Nguyen et al., 2016; Tsuboyama et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Kumar et al., 2018a.

claim: LC3/GABARAP family proteins are not required for STX17 recruitment according to other studies.
source: A previous study reported that LC3/GABARAP family proteins and immunity-related GTPase M (IRGM) are involved in autophagosomal recruitment of STX17 (Kumar et al., 2018a), whereas other studies have shown that LC3/GABARAP family proteins are not required (Nguyen et al., 2016; Tsuboyama et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Nguyen et al., 2016 and Tsuboyama et al., 2016.

claim: Phosphorylation of STX17 and binding to filamin A are important for STX17 recruitment.
source: It has also been recently reported that phosphorylation of STX17 and binding to filamin A are important for STX17 recruitment (Wang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Wang et al., 2023.

claim: STX17 has an N-terminal Habc domain, followed by a SNARE domain, two tandem transmembrane helices, and a short C-terminal region, with both N- and C-terminal ends facing the cytosol.
source: STX17 has an N-terminal Habc domain, followed by a SNARE domain, two tandem transmembrane helices, and a short C-terminal region, with both N- and C-terminal ends facing the cytosol (Figure 1A; Itakura et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 1A, with a citation to Itakura et al., 2012.

claim: A short construct containing only the transmembrane helices and the C-terminal region (STX17TM) behaves similarly to full-length STX17.
source: A short construct containing only the transmembrane helices and the C-terminal region (STX17TM), which behaves similarly to full-length STX17 (Itakura et al., 2012), colocalized with ring-shaped autophagosomes labeled with the general autophagic membrane marker microtubule-associated protein light chain 3B (LC3B; Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Itakura et al., 2012 and supported by data in Figure 1C.

claim: STX17TM colocalized with ring-shaped autophagosomes labeled with LC3B.
source: A short construct containing only the transmembrane helices and the C-terminal region (STX17TM), which behaves similarly to full-length STX17 (Itakura et al., 2012), colocalized with ring-shaped autophagosomes labeled with the general autophagic membrane marker microtubule-associated protein light chain 3B (LC3B; Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The C-terminal region of tail-anchored proteins is generally important for specific membrane targeting.
source: STX17 is a tail-anchored protein, and the C-terminal region of tail-anchored proteins is generally important for specific membrane targeting (Rao et al., 2016; Yagita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to Rao et al., 2016 and Yagita et al., 2013.

claim: Deletion of the C-terminal cytosolic region from STX17TM (TMΔC) resulted in a diffuse cytosolic pattern.
source: Deletion of the C-terminal cytosolic region from STX17TM (TMΔC) resulted in a diffuse cytosolic pattern (Figure 1C), indicating that not only the transmembrane helices but also the C-terminal region of STX17 are required for its proper autophagosomal localization.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Not only the transmembrane helices but also the C-terminal region of STX17 are required for its proper autophagosomal localization.
source: Deletion of the C-terminal cytosolic region from STX17TM (TMΔC) resulted in a diffuse cytosolic pattern (Figure 1C), indicating that not only the transmembrane helices but also the C-terminal region of STX17 are required for its proper autophagosomal localization.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1C.

claim: The amino acid sequence of the C-terminal region of STX17 is not conserved in Drosophila melanogaster and Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: Although the role of STX17 in autophagosome–lysosome fusion is conserved in both Drosophila melanogaster (Dm; Takáts et al., 2013) and Caenorhabditis elegans (Ce; Guo et al., 2014), the amino acid sequence of the C-terminal region is not conserved in these organisms (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: DmSTX17TM and CeSTX17TM were recruited to autophagosomes when expressed in mammalian cells, although less efficiently.
source: Nevertheless, when expressed in mammalian cells, DmSTX17TM and CeSTX17TM were recruited to autophagosomes, although less efficiently (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that recruitment of STX17 does not depend on the specific amino acid sequence in the C-terminal region.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Recruitment of STX17 does not depend on the specific amino acid sequence in the C-terminal region.
source: Nevertheless, when expressed in mammalian cells, DmSTX17TM and CeSTX17TM were recruited to autophagosomes, although less efficiently (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that recruitment of STX17 does not depend on the specific amino acid sequence in the C-terminal region.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Cationic amino acids in the C-terminal region of tail-anchored proteins are important for targeting membranes.
source: In general, cationic amino acids in the C-terminal region of tail-anchored proteins are important for targeting membranes (Borgese et al., 2001; Horie et al., 2002; Yagita et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to Borgese et al., 2001, Horie et al., 2002, and Yagita et al., 2013.

claim: The replacement of lysine and arginine with alanine in the C-terminal region of STX17 impaired autophagosomal localization in a dose-dependent manner.
source: STX17 has cationic amino acids in its C-terminal region, and the replacement of lysine and arginine with alanine impaired autophagosomal localization in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 1A and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The replacement of the C-terminal region with artificial sequences consisting of five residues of positively charged lysine or arginine restored the localization of STX17 to autophagosomes.
source: Moreover, the replacement of the C-terminal region with artificial sequences consisting of five residues of positively charged lysine or arginine, but not negatively charged aspartic acid or uncharged alanine, restored the localization of STX17 to autophagosomes (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The replacement of the C-terminal region with artificial sequences consisting of negatively charged aspartic acid or uncharged alanine did not restore the localization of STX17 to autophagosomes.
source: Moreover, the replacement of the C-terminal region with artificial sequences consisting of five residues of positively charged lysine or arginine, but not negatively charged aspartic acid or uncharged alanine, restored the localization of STX17 to autophagosomes (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Autophagosomal localization of STX17 requires positively charged residues, but not sequence-specific structures, in its C-terminal region.
source: These data suggest that autophagosomal localization of STX17 requires positively charged residues, but not sequence-specific structures, in its C-terminal region.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data in Figures 1D and 1E.

claim: STX17TM was efficiently recruited to liposomes containing anionic phospholipids such as phosphatidylserine (PS), phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PI3P) or PI4P.
source: STX17TM was efficiently recruited to liposomes containing anionic phospholipids such as phosphatidylserine (PS), phosphatidylinositol (PI) 3-phosphate (PI3P) or PI4P (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The association of STX17TM with PI4P-containing membranes was abolished in the presence of 1 M NaCl.
source: The association of STX17TM with PI4P-containing membranes was abolished in the presence of 1 M NaCl (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: STX17 can be recruited to negatively charged membranes via electrostatic interaction independent of the specific lipid species.
source: These data suggest that STX17 can be recruited to negatively charged membranes via electrostatic interaction independent of the specific lipid species.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data in Figures 2A and 2B.

claim: The probe for the most negatively charged membrane (9K0Q) labeled the plasma membrane but not autophagosomes.
source: The probe for the most negatively charged membrane (9K0Q) labeled the plasma membrane, which is known to have a highly negative charge (Li et al., 2014), but not autophagosomes (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D, 2E, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The probes for intermediate (5K4Q and 3K6Q) and weakly (1K8Q) negative charges labeled not only the plasma membrane but also LC3B- and STX17-positive autophagosomes.
source: However, the probes for intermediate (5K4Q and 3K6Q) and weakly (1K8Q) negative charges labeled not only the plasma membrane but also LC3B- and STX17-positive autophagosomes (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D, 2E, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The 1K8Q probe was recruited to not only STX17-positive spherical autophagosomes but also STX17-negative, LC3B-positive elliptic structures that should correspond to unclosed autophagosomes.
source: The 1K8Q probe was recruited to not only STX17-positive spherical autophagosomes but also STX17-negative, LC3B-positive elliptic structures that should correspond to unclosed autophagosomes (Tsuboyama et al., 2016; Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2F, with a citation to Tsuboyama et al., 2016.

claim: The intermediate charge probes (3K6Q and 5K4Q) were recruited to spherical LC3B-positive autophagosomes at almost the same time as STX17.
source: In contrast, the intermediate charge probes (3K6Q and 5K4Q) were recruited to spherical LC3B-positive autophagosomes at almost the same time as STX17 (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Structures positive for ATG5, a marker for unclosed autophagosomes, were labeled with 1K8Q but not with 3K6Q or 5K4Q.
source: Structures positive for ATG5, a marker for unclosed autophagosomes, were labeled with 1K8Q but not with 3K6Q or 5K4Q (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The CERT(PHD) (W33A) mutant, lacking PI4P-binding activity, was not co-localized with STX17TM.
source: The CERT(PHD) (W33A) mutant, lacking PI4P-binding activity, was not co-localized with STX17TM (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A; Sugiki et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, with a citation to Sugiki et al., 2012.

claim: Other PI4P probes, including FAPP(PHD), OSBP(PHD), and P4M-SidMx2, colocalized with STX17TM.
source: Consistently, other PI4P probes, including FAPP(PHD), OSBP(PHD), and P4M-SidMx2, colocalized with STX17TM (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C; Hammond et al., 2014; Platre and Jaillais, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and 2C, with citations to Hammond et al., 2014 and Platre and Jaillais, 2016.

claim: PI4P is an important lipid component of the Golgi complex and the plasma membrane as well as a major regulator of conserved eukaryotic cellular processes.
source: PI4P is an important lipid component of the Golgi complex and the plasma membrane as well as a major regulator of conserved eukaryotic cellular processes (Balla, 2013; Platre et al., 2018; Schink et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to Balla, 2013, Platre et al., 2018, and Schink et al., 2016.

claim: GABARAP-dependent PI4P production by PI4K2A (PI4KIIα) is required for autophagosome–lysosome fusion.
source: In the context of autophagy, it was previously reported that GABARAP-dependent PI4P production by PI4K2A (PI4KIIα) is required for autophagosome–lysosome fusion (Wang et al., 2015), and that PI4KB (PI4KIIIβ) is detected in ATG9A vesicles and early autophagic structures and is furthermore required for autophagosome formation (Judith et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Wang et al., 2015.

claim: PI4KB (PI4KIIIβ) is detected in ATG9A vesicles and early autophagic structures and is required for autophagosome formation.
source: In the context of autophagy, it was previously reported that GABARAP-dependent PI4P production by PI4K2A (PI4KIIα) is required for autophagosome–lysosome fusion (Wang et al., 2015), and that PI4KB (PI4KIIIβ) is detected in ATG9A vesicles and early autophagic structures and is furthermore required for autophagosome formation (Judith et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Judith et al., 2019.

claim: Faint signals of PI4K2A and PI4KB were detected on LC3B-positive structures.
source: Consistently, we detected faint signals of PI4K2A and PI4KB on LC3B-positive structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The PI4P probes (CERT(PHD), FAPP(PHD), OSBP(PHD), and P4M-SidMx2) colocalized with STX17 but not with ATG5.
source: The PI4P probes (CERT(PHD), FAPP(PHD), OSBP(PHD), and P4M-SidMx2) colocalized with STX17 but not with ATG5 (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C), suggesting that PI4P accumulates in mature autophagosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and 2C.

claim: PI4P accumulates in mature autophagosomes.
source: The PI4P probes (CERT(PHD), FAPP(PHD), OSBP(PHD), and P4M-SidMx2) colocalized with STX17 but not with ATG5 (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C), suggesting that PI4P accumulates in mature autophagosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the data in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and 2C.

claim: The signal of the CERT(PHD) probe appeared on LC3B-positive membranes only after the disappearance of the unclosed autophagosome markers ATG5 and WIPI2B.
source: The signal of the CERT(PHD) probe appeared on LC3B-positive membranes only after the disappearance of the unclosed autophagosome markers ATG5 and WIPI2B (Figure 3B and C) and almost at the same time as STX17 localized (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B, 3C, and 3D.

claim: The signal of the CERT(PHD) probe appeared almost at the same time as STX17 localized.
source: The signal of the CERT(PHD) probe appeared on LC3B-positive membranes only after the disappearance of the unclosed autophagosome markers ATG5 and WIPI2B (Figure 3B and C) and almost at the same time as STX17 localized (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The punctate structures of CERT(PHD) were colocalized with LC3B-positive and LAMP1-negative structures in STX17- and YKT6-double-knockdown cells.
source: The punctate structures of CERT(PHD) were still colocalized with LC3B-positive and LAMP1-negative structures in these double-knockdown cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: PI4P accumulation is independent of lysosome fusion.
source: To confirm that PI4P accumulation was independent of autophagosome–lysosome fusion, we evaluated the colocalization among the PI4P probe, LC3B, and LAMP1 in STX17- and YKT6-double-knockdown cells, in which unfused autophagosomes accumulated (Matsui et al., 2018). The punctate structures of CERT(PHD) were still colocalized with LC3B-positive and LAMP1-negative structures in these double-knockdown cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: STX17 recruitment and PI4P enrichment occurred normally in cells lacking all ATG8 family proteins.
source: In addition, STX17 recruitment and PI4P enrichment occurred normally in cells lacking all ATG8 family proteins (LC3A, LC3B, LC3C, GABARAP, GABARAPL1, and GABARAPL2) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2F.

claim: PI4P accumulates in mature autophagosomal membranes independent of lysosome fusion and ATG8 proteins.
source: These results suggest that PI4P accumulates in mature autophagosomal membranes independent of lysosome fusion and ATG8 proteins, and that the kinetics of the accumulation of STX17, the PI4P probes, and the negative charge probes are correlated.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E and 2F.

claim: The kinetics of the accumulation of STX17, the PI4P probes, and the negative charge probes are correlated.
source: These results suggest that PI4P accumulates in mature autophagosomal membranes independent of lysosome fusion and ATG8 proteins, and that the kinetics of the accumulation of STX17, the PI4P probes, and the negative charge probes are correlated.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data presented.

claim: Recombinant mGFP–STX17TM was associated with autophagosomes, but it was significantly impaired by treatment with Sac1PD.
source: Recombinant mGFP–STX17TM was associated with autophagosomes, but it was significantly impaired by treatment with Sac1PD. Phosphatase-dead Sac1PD (C392S) showed no effect (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Phosphatase-dead Sac1PD (C392S) showed no effect on mGFP–STX17TM association with autophagosomes.
source: Recombinant mGFP–STX17TM was associated with autophagosomes, but it was significantly impaired by treatment with Sac1PD. Phosphatase-dead Sac1PD (C392S) showed no effect (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: PI4P is important for autophagosomal recruitment of STX17.
source: These data suggest that PI4P is important for autophagosomal recruitment of STX17.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data in Figure 4D.

claim: In independent simulations using four out of the five predicted STX17TM structures, STX17TM was inserted into the membrane with PI4P (PC:PE:PI4P=70:20:10) within a short time scale of 100 ns.
source: In independent simulations using four out of the five predicted STX17TM structures, STX17TM was inserted into the membrane with PI4P (PC:PE:PI4P=70:20:10) within a short time scale of 100 ns (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: The two transmembrane helices of STX17TM were inserted into the membrane, while the charged C-terminal region remained bound to the membrane surface.
source: The two transmembrane helices were inserted into the membrane, while the charged C-terminal region remained bound to the membrane surface (Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—video 1.

claim: STX17 diffused freely in the solution and was not inserted into the membrane without PI4P (PC:PE = 70:30) in simulations of all five structures.
source: In contrast, STX17 diffused freely in the solution and was not inserted into the membrane without PI4P (PC:PE = 70:30) in simulations of all five structures (Figure 5C and D, Figure 5—video 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C and 5D.

claim: If the membrane contained PI instead of PI4P, STX17TM approached the PI-containing membrane but was not inserted into the membrane.
source: Moreover, if the membrane contained PI instead of PI4P, STX17TM approached the PI-containing membrane but was not inserted into the membrane (Figure 5E and F, Figure 5—video 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5E and 5F.

claim: STX17TM can be readily inserted into PI4P-containing membranes.
source: These results suggest that STX17TM can be readily inserted into PI4P-containing membranes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the simulation data in Figure 5.

claim: The recruitment of STX17 to mature autophagosomes is primarily mediated by the electrostatic interaction between the positively charged C-terminal region of STX17 and negatively charged autophagosomal membranes likely due to accumulation of PI4P.
source: Based on the results of this study, we propose a model in which temporally regulated autophagosome–lysosome fusion involves a dynamic change in electrostatic status during autophagosome maturation; the recruitment of STX17 to mature autophagosomes is primarily mediated by the electrostatic interaction between the positively charged C-terminal region of STX17 and negatively charged autophagosomal membranes likely due to accumulation of PI4P (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as the main conclusion of the study, supported by all the data presented.

claim: STX17 does not localize to all negatively charged membranes (e.g. the plasma membrane).
source: Because STX17 does not localize to all negatively charged membranes (e.g. the plasma membrane), the transmembrane helices appear to also regulate the specificity of target membranes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an observation from the study.

claim: The transmembrane helices of STX17 appear to also regulate the specificity of target membranes.
source: Because STX17 does not localize to all negatively charged membranes (e.g. the plasma membrane), the transmembrane helices appear to also regulate the specificity of target membranes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the observation that STX17 does not localize to all negatively charged membranes.

claim: Both a cationic motif and a nearby membrane-anchored moiety are important for membrane targeting according to the 'coincidence detector' mechanism.
source: This is consistent with the 'coincidence detector' mechanism in which both a cationic motif and a nearby membrane-anchored moiety are important for membrane targeting (Carlton and Cullen, 2005; Yeung and Grinstein, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to Carlton and Cullen, 2005 and Yeung and Grinstein, 2007.

claim: The membrane of autophagosomes become more negatively charged during maturation, most likely through an increase in the PI4P content of their membranes.
source: A striking finding of this study is that the membrane of autophagosomes become more negatively charged during maturation, most likely through an increase in the PI4P content of their membranes, although we do not exclude the possible involvement of other negatively charged molecules.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a main finding of the study.

claim: The authors do not exclude the possible involvement of other negatively charged molecules in the increase in negative charge of autophagosomal membranes.
source: A striking finding of this study is that the membrane of autophagosomes become more negatively charged during maturation, most likely through an increase in the PI4P content of their membranes, although we do not exclude the possible involvement of other negatively charged molecules.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a caveat to the main finding.

claim: PI3P is dephosphorylated to PI during autophagosome formation or maturation.
source: It was reported that PI3P is dephosphorylated to PI during autophagosome formation or maturation (Allen et al., 2020; Cebollero et al., 2012; Taguchi-Atarashi et al., 2010), and that the PI3P effectors DFCP1 and WIPI family proteins are not detected on mature autophagosomes (Koyama-Honda et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to Allen et al., 2020, Cebollero et al., 2012, and Taguchi-Atarashi et al., 2010.

claim: The PI3P effectors DFCP1 and WIPI family proteins are not detected on mature autophagosomes.
source: It was reported that PI3P is dephosphorylated to PI during autophagosome formation or maturation (Allen et al., 2020; Cebollero et al., 2012; Taguchi-Atarashi et al., 2010), and that the PI3P effectors DFCP1 and WIPI family proteins are not detected on mature autophagosomes (Koyama-Honda et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Koyama-Honda et al., 2013.

claim: WIPI2B and the PI3P reporter GFP–2×FYVE were not detected on PI4P-enriched structures.
source: In fact, we did not detect WIPI2B and the PI3P reporter GFP–2×FYVE on PI4P-enriched structures (Figure 3C) and STX17-positive structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The amount of PI4P produced during autophagosome maturation is likely to be higher than that of PI3P in the early stages.
source: Considering the change in autophagosomal membrane charge, the amount of PI4P produced during autophagosome maturation is likely to be higher than that of PI3P in the early stages.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the data.

claim: Immature autophagosomal membranes may have slight negative charges.
source: Our data of the 1K8Q probe suggest that immature autophagosomal membranes may also have slight negative charges (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the data in Figure 2F.

claim: The source of the negative charge of immature autophagosomes may be derived from low levels of PI4P, which is undetectable by the PI4P probes and/or other negatively charged lipids such as PI and PS.
source: Although the source of the negative charge of immature autophagosomes is currently unknown, it may be derived from low levels of PI4P, which is undetectable by the PI4P probes and/or other negatively charged lipids such as PI and PS (Schmitt et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation with a citation to Schmitt et al., 2022.

claim: PI4KB regulates the early stage of autophagosome formation through interaction with ATG9A.
source: It was reported that PI4KB regulates the early stage of autophagosome formation through interaction with ATG9A (Judith et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Judith et al., 2019.

claim: PI4K2A is recruited to autophagosomes by binding to the ATG8 family proteins GABARAP and GABARAPL1 and produces PI4P in the autophagosomal membranes.
source: It was also reported that PI4K2A is recruited to autophagosomes by binding to the ATG8 family proteins GABARAP and GABARAPL1 and produces PI4P in the autophagosomal membranes (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Wang et al., 2015.

claim: The knockdown of PI4K2A resulted in the accumulation of abnormally enlarged autophagosomes, presumably owing to a defect in autophagosome–lysosome fusion.
source: Furthermore, the knockdown of PI4K2A resulted in the accumulation of abnormally enlarged autophagosomes, presumably owing to a defect in autophagosome–lysosome fusion (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Wang et al., 2015.

claim: Autophagosomal membranes contain PI4P in the cytoplasmic leaflets of the outer and inner membranes.
source: Indeed, a freeze-fracture replica labeling study showed that autophagosomal membranes contain PI4P in the cytoplasmic leaflets of the outer and inner membranes (Kurokawa et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Kurokawa et al., 2019.

claim: The knockdown of PI4KIIα in Drosophila blocked autophagic flux at a late step of autophagy in the fat body.
source: Very recently, it was reported that the knockdown of PI4KIIα in Drosophila blocked autophagic flux at a late step of autophagy in the fat body (Liu et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Liu et al., 2023.

claim: The knockdown of PI4KIIα in Drosophila did not inhibit STX17 recruitment.
source: Liu et al. also showed that the knockdown of PI4KIIα in Drosophila did not inhibit STX17 recruitment.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a finding from Liu et al.

claim: PI 4-kinases may function redundantly.
source: This may be because PI 4-kinases function redundantly.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation to explain why genetic depletion of PI4P did not work.

claim: Surface charge is now recognized as one of the key physical properties of cellular membranes.
source: Surface charge, which is now recognized as one of the key physical properties of cellular membranes, regulates various biological processes (Yeung and Grinstein, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Yeung and Grinstein, 2007.

claim: The negatively charged plasma membrane, where anionic phospholipids such as PI(4,5)P2 and PS are enriched, recruits positively charged proteins, including K-Ras and Rac1.
source: For example, the negatively charged plasma membrane, where anionic phospholipids such as PI(4,5)P2 and PS are enriched, recruits positively charged proteins, including K-Ras and Rac1 (Bigay and Antonny, 2012; Heo et al., 2006; Li et al., 2014; Platre et al., 2018; Yeung et al., 2008; Yeung et al., 2006), some of which are released from the membrane when the negative charge of the surface is reduced during phagocytosis (Yeung et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with multiple citations.

claim: Some positively charged proteins are released from the plasma membrane when the negative charge of the surface is reduced during phagocytosis.
source: For example, the negatively charged plasma membrane, where anionic phospholipids such as PI(4,5)P2 and PS are enriched, recruits positively charged proteins, including K-Ras and Rac1 (Bigay and Antonny, 2012; Heo et al., 2006; Li et al., 2014; Platre et al., 2018; Yeung et al., 2008; Yeung et al., 2006), some of which are released from the membrane when the negative charge of the surface is reduced during phagocytosis (Yeung et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Yeung et al., 2006.

claim: PI4P can be structurally recognized by a series of PI4P-binding domain-containing proteins.
source: Generally, PI4P can be structurally recognized by a series of PI4P-binding domain-containing proteins (Laczkó-Dobos et al., 2024; Moravcevic et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to Laczkó-Dobos et al., 2024 and Moravcevic et al., 2012.

claim: PI4P can generate a negatively charged electrostatic field and recruit positively charged proteins independent of specific amino acid motifs.
source: However, recent studies suggest that PI4P can also generate a negatively charged electrostatic field and recruit positively charged proteins independent of specific amino acid motifs (Hammond et al., 2012; Simon et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to Hammond et al., 2012 and Simon et al., 2016.

claim: PI4P recruits the polar auxin transport regulator PINOID and other signaling molecules to the cell plate in plants.
source: Examples of the role of PI4P in electrostatic signature include the recruitment of the polar auxin transport regulator PINOID and other signaling molecules to the cell plate in plants (Simon et al., 2016) the recruitment of D6 protein kinase (Barbosa et al., 2016), NPH3 (Reuter et al., 2021), and the exocyst complex (Synek et al., 2021) to the plasma membrane in plants; the recruitment of Lgl and Dlg proteins, which function in cell polarity and tumorigenesis, to the plasma membrane in Drosophila (Darden et al., 1993; Lu et al., 2021); and the recruitment of NLRP3 to the disassembled trans-Golgi network during inflammasome activation in mammals (Chen and Chen, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Simon et al., 2016.

claim: Autophagosomal PI4P serves as a regulator of surface charge.
source: In the present study, we showed that autophagosomal PI4P also serves as a regulator of surface charge.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion of the study.

claim: Electrostatic maturation would be an efficient way for the function of autophagosomes to switch from sequestration to fusion with lysosomes.
source: Given that the function of elongating unclosed autophagosomes (i.e. sequestration) and mature closed autophagosomes (i.e. fusion with lysosomes) differs despite using seemingly the same membrane, electrostatic maturation would be an efficient way for the function to switch.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion of the study.

claim: If lysosomes were to fuse with intermediate unclosed structures and their inner membrane is degraded, then harmful lysosomal enzymes would leak out into the cytosol.
source: If lysosomes were to fuse with intermediate unclosed structures and their inner membrane is degraded, then harmful lysosomal enzymes would leak out into the cytosol.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a rationale for temporal regulation of autophagosome-lysosome fusion.

claim: Temporal regulation of autophagosome–lysosome fusion is achieved in mammals by two mechanisms.
source: This temporal regulation of autophagosome–lysosome fusion is achieved in mammals by two mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as established knowledge.

claim: ULK1 is dissociated from autophagosomes at the time of autophagosome completion.
source: The other is the activation of YKT6, a conserved autophagosomal SNARE (Matsui et al., 2018), which is kept inactivated by ULK1 (a homolog of yeast Atg1)-mediated phosphorylation until the completion of autophagosome formation (ULK1/Atg1 is dissociated at this time; Barz et al., 2020; Essmann et al., 1995; Sánchez-Martín et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations.

claim: The role of STX17 in autophagosome–lysosome fusion is conserved in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: Although the role of STX17 in autophagosome–lysosome fusion is conserved in both Drosophila melanogaster (Dm; Takáts et al., 2013) and Caenorhabditis elegans (Ce; Guo et al., 2014), the amino acid sequence of the C-terminal region is not conserved in these organisms (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Takáts et al., 2013.

claim: The role of STX17 in autophagosome–lysosome fusion is conserved in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: Although the role of STX17 in autophagosome–lysosome fusion is conserved in both Drosophila melanogaster (Dm; Takáts et al., 2013) and Caenorhabditis elegans (Ce; Guo et al., 2014), the amino acid sequence of the C-terminal region is not conserved in these organisms (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Guo et al., 2014.

claim: The plasma membrane is known to have a highly negative charge.
source: The probe for the most negatively charged membrane (9K0Q) labeled the plasma membrane, which is known to have a highly negative charge (Li et al., 2014), but not autophagosomes (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Li et al., 2014.

claim: LysoTracker signals appear ring-shaped until inner membrane degradation.
source: This was followed by the appearance of LysoTracker signals (note that LysoTracker signals have been previously observed to appear ring-shaped until inner membrane degradation Tsuboyama et al., 2016; Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Tsuboyama et al., 2016 and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Unfused autophagosomes accumulated in STX17- and YKT6-double-knockdown cells.
source: To confirm that PI4P accumulation was independent of autophagosome–lysosome fusion, we evaluated the colocalization among the PI4P probe, LC3B, and LAMP1 in STX17- and YKT6-double-knockdown cells, in which unfused autophagosomes accumulated (Matsui et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Matsui et al., 2018.

claim: Mature autophagosomes prior to fusion with lysosomes were isolated from STX17 knockout (KO) cells.
source: Mature autophagosomes prior to fusion with lysosomes were isolated from STX17 knockout (KO) cells (Figure 4B, Fraction #1; Matsui et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B, with a citation to Matsui et al., 2018.
